newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Aug single-family home sales rose 4.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Aug single-family home sales rose 4.7 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department reported sales of new single-family homes, seasonally adjusted, with percent changes from prior months (numbers in 1,000s).
- Pct--- Aug July--Rev from June--Rev from
-By Region: Pct--- Aug July--Rev from June--Rev from
Total sales of single-family homes in August were up 17.7 percent from an annualized rate of 707,000 units in August last year.
In 1,000s: Aug July--Rev from June--Rev from
Actual Units Sold 74 67 66 65 65
Note-Actual number of new single-family units sold is not seasonally adjusted.
Wall Street economists had expected August single-family home sales at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 744,000 units.
The department also revised monthly percent changes of total sales, seasonally adjusted, from prior months as follows:
- July-Rev from June--Rev from May--Rev from
Total Units 8.3 7.9 Unch -1.8 -0.8 -0.1
The annualized sales rate for May was revised to 734,000 units from 739,000.
The August supply of homes for sale fell to 5.3 months' worth from a revised 5.9 months' worth in July that was previously reported as 5.8 months.
The inventory of houses for sale at the end of August was 355,000 units, off from a revised 379,000 units in July that was previously reported as 365,000 units.
The department said that the August annualized sales rate of 832,000 units was the highest since April 1986 when the rate was 857,000 units.
The Midwest annualized sales rate of 196,000 units was the highest since December 1993, when it was 206,000.
The August average home sale price of $157,800 was the lowest since January 1996 when it was $155,300, the department said.
August was the eighth consecutive month that new homes sold at a rate above 700,000 units.
